data.title: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $62K: What Should You Do?
data.description:
Bitcoin price has fallen below $62,000 for the first time since early July, extending a brutal November selloff as institutional investors pull billions from the market. BTC touched $61,270 just now, before recovering slightly to trade around $61,700.

Bitcoin price has now lost more than 10% over seven days, with selling pressure spreading across equities, precious metals and other risk assets. Yesterday’s $582.2 million outflow from US spot Bitcoin ETFs added another blow, bringing November withdrawals close to $3.5 billion.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest single-day outflow since launching. The same session saw $727 million in crypto liquidations, with bullish traders absorbing most of the damage.

Institutional demand is weakening, leveraged buyers are being forced out, and the Federal Reserve’s increasingly hawkish outlook is making speculative assets less attractive.

Bitcoin is now approaching $60,000, a level that could determine if the correction finds a floor or develops into something uglier.Xrp (XRP)24h7d30d1yAll timeBitcoin ETF Exodus and $727M Liquidations Put Bulls on the Defensive

The ETF withdrawals are arguably the biggest concern for Bitcoin holders right now. Spot Bitcoin ETFs became an important source of institutional demand after launching in January 2024. Their buying helped absorb available supply and gave traditional investors a regulated route into the market.

That demand is now moving in the opposite direction. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost more than $1.1 billion this week alone. November’s cumulative withdrawals have approached $3.5 billion.Bitcoin ETF Flows,

The pressure extends beyond ETFs. Rising Treasury yields and expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase in December have encouraged investors to reduce exposure to assets that offer no regular income.

Meanwhile, derivatives traders are taking heavy losses. CoinGlass data showed more than $700 million in liquidations across crypto markets over 24 hours. Long positions accounted for 86% of the total.

Bitcoin itself recorded nearly $202 million in liquidations, with bullish traders suffering the majority of forced closures.

This creates a difficult environment for buyers. Falling prices trigger liquidations, which create additional selling pressure and push prices lower. The reduction in open interest also suggests excessive leverage is being flushed from the market.

Discover: The Best Token PresalesBitcoin Price Prediction: $60K Breakdown or Relief Rally?

The immediate battle is around $60,000. Bitcoin needs to reclaim $62,000 and establish support above it before bulls can confidently argue that the latest breakdown was temporary.

There are three possible scenarios:

Scenario 1: Bitcoin loses $60K and heads toward $58K or $53K.BTC USD,

This is the bearish outcome. A decisive break below $60,000 could trigger another wave of stop-loss orders and leveraged liquidations.

The next downside area sits around $58,000, while more aggressive technical projections point toward $53,700.

The daily chart offers little encouragement for bulls. Bitcoin trades below its major moving averages, while bearish momentum continues to dominate. A sustained recovery in ETF flows would become increasingly important to prevent further deterioration.

Scenario 2: Bitcoin stabilizes between $60K and $62K.BTC USD,

This would give buyers time to absorb available supply without immediately reversing the entire November decline.

The liquidation wave has already removed considerable leverage from the market. If ETF withdrawals begin slowing, Bitcoin could establish a trading range before attempting another recovery.

But sideways trading alone would not confirm a bottom. Buyers need to demonstrate that they can defend support through multiple sessions.

Scenario 3: Bitcoin reclaims $62K and launches a relief rally.BTC USD,

A recovery above $62,000 would provide the first meaningful sign that sellers are losing control. A move toward $65,000 would then become possible, followed by resistance around $68,000.

Consistent ETF inflows, improving market sentiment, and a weaker dollar would strengthen this scenario. Without those developments, any rebound risks becoming another opportunity for sellers to exit.Should Bitcoin Holders Sell, Hold or Buy the Dip?

For existing holders, the decision depends heavily on their entry price, investment horizon, and exposure. Long-term holders who bought substantially below current prices have more room to withstand volatility. Selling simply because Bitcoin crossed a psychological threshold risks locking in profits or losses without knowing whether the broader investment thesis has changed.

However, investors holding leveraged positions face a different problem. Falling prices can trigger forced liquidations regardless of their long-term convictions. Reducing leverage and protecting available capital should take priority over waiting for a rebound.

For buyers, the temptation to buy the dip is understandable. Bitcoin is considerably cheaper than it was just weeks ago, but cheaper does not automatically mean undervalued.

Buying in stages rather than committing an entire allocation around $61,000 offers more flexibility if the market tests $58,000 or even $53,700.

Bitcoin price remains vulnerable to another leg down. The $60,000 level is no longer just a psychological milestone. It is where the next major battle between buyers and sellers.

data.title: Baltic index inches down on lower capesize, supramax vessel rates
data.description:
The Baltic Exchange's main sea freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, eased on Friday and logged a weekly fall, as declines in the capesize and supramax vessel segments overshadowed modest gains in the panamax category.

  • The main Baltic index , tracking capesize, panamax and supramax vessels' rates, edged lower by 3 points, or 0.1%, to 2,898 points

  • The index marked a 2.8% loss for the week

  • The capesize index (.BACI) fell by 12 points, or 0.3%, to 4,502 points, and posted a 4.6% weekly decline

  • Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-metric-ton cargoes including iron ore and coal, decreased by $114 to $37,324

  • Iron ore futures rose on Friday on hopes of year-end restocking by steel mills, though the contracts posted a weekly loss after breaking through previous lows earlier in the week amid weak demand and high port stocks

  • The panamax index (.BPNI) inched up by 8 points at 2,140 points, its highest level since October 22, and logged a weekly rise of 1%

  • Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, rose by $76 to $19,264

  • The supramax index (.BSIS), for smaller vessels, lost 4 points, or 0.2%, to 1,810 points, and posted a 1.4% weekly drop

data.title: Britain’s most realistic EU future looks Swiss
data.description:
By Jon Sindreu

Despite Brussels’ dislike for piecemeal deals, the UK-EU ‘Brexit reset’ is another step towards a Swiss-style web of agreements. That might boost GDP by half as much as full membership. But it may be the most plausible route to growth while trying to rejoin looks risky.

Full view will be published shortly.

Follow Jon Sindreu on X and LinkedIn.

CONTEXT NEWS

Britain and the European Union agreed on November 20 in a summit in Brussels to scrap the certificates and controls currently required for cross-border trade in animals, plants and related products, as well as to align both economies' emission trading schemes and to launch a youth experience programme that would allow 100,000 young Europeans to travel, work and study in the United Kingdom, and vice versa. Both parties still need to agree over the coming months on how much to lower tuition fees for EU students attending British universities.

About Provexis plc

AIM quoted Provexis is focused on the development, licensing and sales of its proprietary, scientifically-proven Fruitflow® heart-health functional food ingredient.

Fruitflow is a natural, breakthrough ingredient that helps with platelet aggregation. This helps promote normal blood flow and circulation, which in turn benefits cardiovascular health. Fruitflow helps the platelets to circulate freely and smoothly throughout your blood, without sticking to one another or to the blood vessels themselves. Freely flowing blood helps reduce stress on your cardiovascular system.

Fruitflow is a highly concentrated form of bioactives which is lycopene-free and contains over 30 known anti-platelet compounds. Published clinical studies have shown that Fruitflow works to maintain healthy blood flow in a similar way to 75mg aspirin but with a milder and reversible action; Fruitflow has a similar antiplatelet effect to a single dose of aspirin - but when taken daily, it has none of aspirin’s side effects.

The science behind Fruitflow has been validated by leading peer review publications and regulatory authorities. Fruitflow is the only natural antiplatelet to have a health claim approved by the European Food Safety Authority, stating that 150mg of Fruitflow ‘helps maintain normal platelet aggregation, which contributes to healthy blood flow’.

Fruitflow has a number of specific health benefits which have been reflected in separate patent filings for the use of Fruitflow in:

  • mitigating exercise-induced inflammation;
  • managing blood pressure;
  • protecting against the adverse effects of air pollution on the body’s cardiovascular system. Laboratory work has shown that Fruitflow can reduce the platelet activation caused by airborne particulate matter, such as that from diesel emissions, by approximately one third; and
  • conferring health benefits in modulating the gut microbiome of humans, to include a reduction in TMAO, following the completion of a successful human study which is further detailed here www.dsm-firmenich.com/en/businesses/health-nutrition-care/news/press-releases/2023-01-20-new-study-reveals-dsms-fruitflow-activates-gut-heart.html.

Provexis sells a high quality dietary supplement product containing Fruitflow and Omega-3 from its website www.fruitflowplus.com on a mail order basis. The product is also available to purchase from Amazon.co.uk.

Provexis has been working with BYHEALTH, a circa £2bn listed Chinese dietary supplement business, for more than ten years to support the planned launch of a number of Fruitflow based products in the Chinese market. Clinical studies conducted in China are typically required to obtain the necessary regulatory clearances in China, and a significant investment in eight separate Fruitflow studies has been undertaken at BYHEALTH’s expense. Completed studies have shown excellent results in use for Fruitflow, and they provide strong evidence for the efficacy of Fruitflow on platelet function.

The Chinese regulatory system for functional health food ingredients, such as Fruitflow, is governed by the State Administration for Market Regulation (the ‘SAMR’) and it is based on a defined list of permitted health function claims which brand owners are permitted to use on product labels.

In August 2023 the Company was delighted to report that BYHEALTH had submitted: i) the first application for a new permitted health function claim and ii) some related product registration applications.

The significance of these major developments for Fruitflow in China is further outlined here www.nutraingredients-asia.com/Article/2023/09/05/china-set-to-approve-new-function-claims-for-health-foods. BYHEALTH has noted that it has been working on the project since 2015, with ‘tens of millions of funds’ (RMB) invested by BYHEALTH in the research and development work.

Provexis was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in Reading, Berkshire. Provexis’ shares are traded on the AIM market of the London Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol PXS.

For further information, please visit www.provexis.com and www.fruitflowplus.com.

20 November 2026

The Smarter Web Company PLC

(“The Smarter Web Company” or the "Company")

PDMR/Director Dealing

The Smarter Web Company announces that on 20 November 2026, Andrew Webley, Chief Executive Officer, together with his spouse and children, purchased an aggregate of 148,597 ordinary shares of £0.001 each in the Company (“Ordinary Shares”), for an aggregate cost of £51,510, as detailed in the PDMR Form below.

Following these purchases, Andrew Webley together with his spouse and children are interested in, in aggregate, 27,713,731 Ordinary Shares, representing approximately 7.33 per cent of the Company’s issued Ordinary Share capital.

About The Smarter Web Company

The Company owns and operates digital services businesses focused on web design, development and digital marketing. The Company serves more than 500 client websites across a diverse range of sectors and generates a significant and growing proportion of its revenue through long-term client relationships and retained service arrangements.

The Company's strategy combines the operation and acquisition of cash-generative businesses with a Bitcoin treasury policy designed to build long-term Shareholder value (the "Bitcoin Treasury Policy"). The Directors believe that Bitcoin will form a significant part of the future global financial system and have therefore adopted this Bitcoin Treasury Policy under which Bitcoin is the Company's primary treasury reserve asset.

The primary objectives of the Bitcoin Treasury Policy are to support the Company's overall capital position and to seek to increase Bitcoin per Ordinary Share over time, with a secondary objective of increasing the total number of Bitcoin held on the Company's balance sheet. The Directors believe that growing Bitcoin per share while simultaneously increasing the scale of the Company's Bitcoin holdings creates a stronger balance sheet and supports the Company as a whole in providing a more attractive investment proposition for existing and prospective Shareholders.

As the strength of the balance sheet increases, the Company believes it can access larger pools of capital on favourable terms, provided such capital raising activity remains accretive to Bitcoin per Ordinary Share. This creates a cycle in which capital can be deployed to pursue strategic acquisitions and acquire additional Bitcoin that strengthen the Company's operating businesses, increase revenues and cash generation, and further enhance the overall strength of the Company.

The Ordinary Shares are admitted to listing on the equity shares (commercial companies) category of the Official List and to trading on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange under the ticker SWC and are quoted on the OTCQB Venture Market in the U.S. under the ticker TSWCF. The Ordinary Shares can also be traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under the ticker 3M8.

The Preferred Shares are admitted to listing on the non-equity shares and non-voting equity shares category of the Official List and to trading on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange under the ticker MORE and are quoted on the OTCQB Venture Market in the U.S. under the ticker MORPF.

Please also see "The 10 Year Plan", announced by the Company via a regulatory information service at 7.00 a.m. on 28 April 2025 and available on the Company's website: https://www.smarterwebcompany.co.uk

Follow the Company on X: https://x.com/smarterwebuk

The Smarter Web Company's Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) is 213800VQO9FUG4PZMP73.

The Directors of the Company accept responsibility for the contents of this announcement.

Important Notice

The Smarter Web Company PLC holds treasury reserves and surplus cash in Bitcoin. Bitcoin is a type of cryptocurrency or cryptoasset. Whilst the Board of Directors of the Company considers holding Bitcoin to be in the best interests of the Company, the Board remains aware that the financial regulator in the UK (the Financial Conduct Authority or FCA) considers investment in Bitcoin to be high risk. An investment in the Company is not an investment in Bitcoin, either directly or by proxy. However, the Board of Directors of the Company considers Bitcoin to be an appropriate store of value and growth for the Company's reserves and, accordingly, the Company is materially exposed to Bitcoin. Such an approach is innovative, and the Board of Directors of the Company wishes to be clear and transparent with prospective and actual investors in the Company on the Company's position in this regard.

The Company is neither authorised nor regulated in the conduct of its business by the FCA, and there is currently limited regulation of cryptocurrencies (such as Bitcoin) in the UK. As with most other investments, the value of Bitcoin can go down as well as up, and therefore the value of the Company's Bitcoin holdings can fluctuate. The Company may not be able to realise its Bitcoin exposure for the same as it paid in the first place or even for the value the Company ascribes to its Bitcoin positions due to these market movements. An investment in the Company is not protected by the UK's Financial Ombudsman Service or the Financial Services Compensation Scheme.

Nevertheless, the Board of Directors of the Company has taken the decision to invest in Bitcoin, and in doing so is mindful of the special risks Bitcoin presents to the Company's financial position. These risks include (but are not limited to): (i) the value of Bitcoin can be highly volatile, with value dropping as quickly as it can rise. Investors in Bitcoin must be prepared to lose all money invested in Bitcoin; (ii) the Bitcoin market is largely unregulated. There is a risk of losing money due to risks such as cyber-attacks, financial crime and counterparty failure; (iii) the Company may not be able to buy or sell its Bitcoin at will. The ability to buy or sell Bitcoin depends on various factors, including the supply and demand in the market at the relevant time. Operational failings such as technology outages, cyber-attacks and comingling of funds could cause unwanted delay; and (iv) cryptoassets are characterised in some quarters by high degrees of fraud, money laundering and financial crime. In addition, there is a perception in some quarters that cyber-attacks are prominent, which can lead to theft of holdings or ransom demands. The Board of Directors of the Company does not subscribe to such a negative view, especially in relation to Bitcoin. However, prospective investors in the Company are encouraged to do their own research before investing.

data.title: Krista Rogalski Elevated To Director, Technology Talent Acquisition At Disney
data.description:
Rogalski Steps Into The Role After More Than A Decade At Disney, With Experience Across Technology Recruitment, Hiring Strategy And Talent Leadership

The Walt Disney Company has elevated Krista Rogalski to Director, Technology Talent Acquisition (IA), effective October 2026. Rogalski brings more than a decade of experience at the company, having progressed through multiple roles in technology recruitment and talent acquisition leadership.

From Sourcing To Leadership

Rogalski joined Disney in December 2015 as a Technical Talent Sourcer. She subsequently served as Technical Recruiter, Senior Technical Recruiter, Manager, Technical Talent Acquisition and Senior Manager, Technology Talent Acquisition before taking up her current position.

In her most recent role, which she held from May 2022 to October 2026, Rogalski led talent acquisition teams supporting technology, media and other business functions. Her responsibilities included aligning recruitment strategies with business priorities, developing recruiting managers and improving hiring processes.

Focus On Hiring Strategy

As Senior Manager, Rogalski worked with senior business and human resources leaders to assess workforce requirements and establish recruiting priorities. She also focused on interview standardisation, candidate assessment, recruiter development and the use of recruitment data to inform decisions.

Her work included evaluating recruiting operating models and improving collaboration across talent acquisition and human resources teams to respond to changing business requirements.

Experience Beyond Disney

Before joining Disney, Rogalski worked at Kforce Inc., where she held Technical Recruiter and Technology VMO Recruiter positions between March 2014 and December 2015.

She previously spent more than five years at Bridgewater Associates, working in technology recruiting and project management from November 2008 to December 2013. Earlier in her career, she served as a Diversity Specialist at Panasonic between July 2002 and August 2008.

Education And Expertise

Rogalski holds a bachelor's degree in Business Administration, with a specialisation in Management, from William Paterson University of New Jersey.

Her career spans technology recruitment, recruiting operations, team development and workforce planning. In her new role, she brings experience in aligning talent acquisition practices with business needs and managing recruitment teams across multiple functions.

data.title: Apollo Hospitals Hits Record High As Macquarie Double Upgrades Stock, Sees 20% Upside
data.description:
Shares of Apollo Hospitals surged more than 5 per cent to a fresh all-time high on Friday after global brokerage Macquarie upgraded the stock by two notches and sharply raised its target price, citing improving earnings prospects, easing valuation concerns and healthy capacity expansion.

Macquarie upgraded Apollo Hospitals to ‘Outperform’ from ‘Underperform’ and increased its price target to Rs 10,500 from Rs 6,230, indicating a potential upside of 20.2 per cent from Thursday’s closing price.

The brokerage believes consensus earnings estimates have bottomed out, while the stock’s valuations have become more reasonable. It also noted that the initial profitability pressure associated with the hospital operator’s bed expansion programme is largely reflected in expectations, with newly added capacity witnessing a healthy ramp-up.

The upgrade follows Apollo Hospitals’ stronger-than-expected performance in the September quarter, when both revenue and profit surpassed market estimates.

Q2 Earnings Beat Street Expectations

Apollo Hospitals reported a 33.6 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 660 crore, exceeding analysts’ expectations of Rs 632 crore.

Revenue grew 23 per cent to Rs 7,615 crore from Rs 6,189 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, ahead of the Street estimate of Rs 7,515 crore.

Operating performance also improved, with earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rising 28.8 per cent to Rs 1,191 crore from Rs 925 crore a year earlier. The figure was above the market estimate of Rs 1,160 crore.

EBITDA margin expanded to 15.6 per cent from 14.9 per cent in the year-ago period, surpassing analysts’ expectations of 15.4 per cent.

The hospital operator also reported stronger operational metrics. Occupancy improved to 73 per cent from 69 per cent a year earlier, while inpatient volumes increased 14 per cent. Average revenue per occupied bed rose 8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,86,880.

Stock Extends Gains For Second Consecutive Month

Apollo Hospitals shares climbed as much as 5.3 per cent to touch a record high of Rs 9,205 during Friday’s session. The stock subsequently pared some gains and was trading 4.6 per cent higher at Rs 9,138.

The rally has extended the stock’s November gains to around 8 per cent, following a 3.5 per cent rise in October. This marks its strongest monthly performance since February 2026, when the shares advanced 12.4 per cent.

Apollo Hospitals has recorded gains in seven of the 11 months of 2026 so far, with its year-to-date return reaching 28.5 per cent.
